#### For chain teams and delegators

For chain teams

##### Launch.

Add us to your genesis set, from your first testnet onward.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/aditya-encapsulate/30min)

What you get

1. Upgrades run within minutes of notice, not days
2. On call around the clock, in your Discord, not a ticket queue
3. We find the breakages on testnet so mainnet does not
4. Dashboards and tooling built for your community, not ours

For delegators

##### Stake.

Delegate to a validator that is already running.

[View networks](https://encapsulate.xyz/networks)

What you get

1. Zero slashes, across every validator we have run
2. Your keys never leave your wallet
3. Low commission, so more of the reward stays yours
4. Redundant nodes in two regions, so downtime never costs you rewards

Why stake with us

02

#### Playbooks

A playbook for every network. What each one does to a machine.

01

Prepare the server

Environment and dependencies, the same on every host.

02

Firewall

Opens only the ports the node needs, and closes the rest.

03

User and directories

The node runs as its own user, in its own directories.

04

Configuration

Config files and genesis, templated for the network and node type.

05

Keys from Vault

Validator keys come from HashiCorp Vault at deploy time, so they are never kept in the repository.

06

Binaries

Fetches the pinned release of the node and its tools.

07

Service

A systemd unit, restarted only when something changed.

## Security

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/security

How we hold keys, run machines and handle upgrades: the rules we hold ourselves to.

Encapsulate · Security

Keys & isolation

### The part that only shows when it fails.

Key management, slashing protection and host isolation — the work you never see until the day you need it.

[Book a call](https://cal.com/aditya-encapsulate/30min)

[How we secure it](https://encapsulate.xyz/security#block-3e0e800a5138816a82dbd9653ac6e94c)

Defence in depth

Scroll ↓

Security and operations · 01

#### How we run a validator.

Nine commitments, the same on every chain we join. Each is a practice we can show you, not a figure we would have to keep proving.

1h

for an emergency release

2×2

regions and providers

0

slashing events since 2020

[Book a call](https://cal.com/aditya-encapsulate/30min)

Uptime

Alerting pages a person, not a dashboard. A hot standby takes over automatically, and the switch is a signing handoff — blocks, not minutes.

Upgrades

Every release runs on our testnet node first, then mainnet. Routine releases inside 24 hours of the announcement; emergency releases inside one hour.

Responsiveness

A named engineer and a shared channel with your team from day one, plus a security address that reaches the on-call rotation. Outreach is answered the same day.

Testnet

We join at testnet and keep the testnet node for as long as we hold the mainnet seat, so the chain's early weeks are ours too.

Incidents

If something on our side affects your chain, we publish a post-mortem in your validator channel: what happened, when we knew, and what we changed.

Diversity

Bare metal across two regions and two providers, chosen per chain against the validator set's current map so we never add to a concentration you are trying to reduce. We are based in India, where few validators are — a seat with us is geography most sets do not have.

Metrics

Prometheus endpoints scoped to your team, so you watch the same numbers we do. A bridge or archive node where the chain wants one. Nothing on trust.

Conduct

Stock binaries, no MEV side-channels, a separate full node for anything public, KYB documents ready, and commission set per chain under that chain's cap.

Contribution

Dashboards, an Ansible repository, alert rules and guides, published for the chains we run — so the next operator starts further along than we did.

Access · 02

#### Two ways to reach a validator. One door for each.

Blocks reach it through sentries we run. People reach it through a private network with no public route. Nothing else reaches it at all.

01

A block

Arrives at both regions' sentries on one port and reaches both validators over private peering; the standby stays in sync. Only the live one asks the cosigners, who agree two of three, and the signed vote leaves the way it came.

Private tailnet · firewall on every host, inbound denied by default

p2p

rpc

peers

ssh

logs

out · dials both · 2 of 3

Outside

The internet

Peers, RPC clients, everything inbound

Region 1

Sentries

Replaceable, re-addressable

Region 2

Public reads

Full nodes

RPC, indexing. Hold nothing.

Outside

An engineer

Tagged laptop, hardware key

Primary · signing

Validator A

Bare metal. Nothing else on it.

Standby · in sync

Validator B

Bare metal. Waiting for the cosigners.

Shard 1

Cosigner

Own host. No inbound.

Shard 2

Shard 3

Every host

Monitoring

auditd, Wazuh, Loki, alerts to a person

How it is run · 9 rules

pick one

01

Sentry layer

The validator peers only with nodes we run. Public traffic lands on sentries that can be replaced or re-addressed under attack, so a block proposal always reaches the network.

Keys · 03

The key is three shards, 2 of 3, and is never assembled. Each shard sits with a cosigner on its own host with no inbound ports. Every cosigner keeps the high-water mark, so the same height is never signed twice. The keys that move stake are split across people — no one alone can act. And there is no hardware: lose a cosigner and the other two keep signing.

hover a highlighted word

Hover a highlighted word for the full commitment.

Failover · 04

#### Built to lose a data centre and keep signing.

Bare metal, nothing on the host but the validator. Two of everything, in two places, on two providers. Failover is a signing decision measured in blocks.

01

signer → host A

Normal

The signing layer is connected to both hosts and signs on A. B is in sync and idle, on a different provider in a different region.

02

host A unreachable

Region A lost

Provider outage, fibre cut, fire. The cosigners see A stop answering. Nothing else on the network notices yet.

03

signer → host B

Signing from B

Signing moves to B. The high-water mark rules out signing the same height twice, which is what makes the switch safe.

04

host A rejoins · standby

A comes back

It rejoins as the standby. No one touched a key; the ceremony stays where it belongs.

Upgrades and response · 05

#### Routine inside a day. Emergency inside an hour.

Emergency releases are where a validator earns or loses its seat. Our path is the same every time and on every chain, so it is fast when it matters.

Routine release

Inside 24 h

Emergency release

Inside 1 h

Reply to outreach

Same day

On call

24/7 rotation

Channel

Shared with your team

Announcement

We acknowledge in your channel the same day and confirm when we will move — the scheduled point if the chain sets one, otherwise our own window.

Testnet

The new release runs on our testnet validator first. Anything that breaks, breaks there.

Mainnet

Applied by the on-call engineer with a second engineer watching the standby; the standby moves first, so a bad release never takes the live host down.

Confirmation

Signed blocks on the new version, reported back to you. Routine releases inside 24 hours of the announcement; emergency releases inside one.

Slashing and the record · 06

0

Slashing events since 2020, across every validator we have run. On chain and checkable.

What slashing costs a validator

The seat.

Downtime

Missing blocks is a monitoring failure. Small and recoverable on most chains, but delegators see it and foundations count it — which is why alerting pages a person, not a dashboard.

Double-signing

Signing two blocks at one height is almost never an attack; it is a failover done wrong. The penalty is severe and on many chains permanent. The 2-of-3 signature and every cosigner's high-water mark are what rule it out.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our blocks and era points are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

Yes — 1,000 AVAIL to nominate us directly. Nomination pools take 100 AVAIL, but the pool chooses its validators.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. They stay in your wallet — delegation is non-custodial.

How often are rewards paid?

Every era — about 24 hours — once anyone claims the era’s payout; it goes to your stake or your balance, as you chose.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. A whole 4-hour session offline drops a validator from the next election; if over 10% are down, stake is slashed up to 7%.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Unbonding takes 28 days (28 eras); the amount earns nothing meanwhile, then you withdraw it.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our uptime is on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

25 AVAX — the smallest delegation the chain accepts.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. They stay in your wallet — delegation is non-custodial.

How often are rewards paid?

In one sum when your staking period ends, sent to your P-Chain address with your stake.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. If the node is up under 80% of its staking period, the chain pays no rewards; stake is never cut.

Can I unstake at any time?

No. Your AVAX is locked for the period you choose — 2 weeks to 1 year — then returns with its rewards.

### EigenCloud

Delegate in two minutes. Your keys never leave your wallet; rewards are posted weekly, for you to claim.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed attestation wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our AVS registrations and delegated stake are on-chain for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

No. Restake any amount of EIGEN and delegate it to us.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. Your tokens are restaked in EigenLayer’s contracts, and only you can withdraw them.

How often are rewards paid?

Weekly, to a balance you claim in the EigenLayer app — each week becomes claimable about ten days after it ends.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. Nothing delegated to us is slashable today; an AVS can eject an operator that misses work, and its rewards stop.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. A withdrawal waits 14 days in escrow, earning nothing, then you complete it in the EigenLayer app.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

Do you hold my tokens?

No. Your ESP sits in Espresso’s stake table contract on Ethereum; only your address can withdraw it.

How often are rewards paid?

With each block we propose, into a balance you claim on Ethereum.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. The chain pays nothing for blocks we miss; there is no slashing.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Undelegated ESP can be withdrawn after the 7-day exit escrow, with one undelegation pending per validator at a time.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our signing and votes are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

1 IKA — the smallest stake the network accepts.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. They stay in your wallet — delegation is non-custodial.

How often are rewards paid?

Every epoch — about 24 hours — added to your stake.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. If two-thirds of the committee report a validator, the network withholds that epoch’s rewards; stake is never cut.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. After you request it, your IKA can be withdrawn in 12–36 hours, depending on when in the epoch you ask.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our signing is on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

No. Lido pools deposits, so you can stake any amount of ETH.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. Your ETH goes into Lido’s contracts, and you hold stETH, a liquid token, in your own wallet.

How often are rewards paid?

Once a day, around 12:30 UTC — your stETH balance grows, after Lido’s 10% fee.

What happens if you go offline?

Any five of the cluster’s seven operators keep it signing. Downtime is never slashed; a missed attestation costs about what it would have paid.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Lido’s withdrawal queue usually takes 1–5 days, without rewards meanwhile — or swap stETH for ETH at market price.

## Mina staking

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/networks/mina

Stake MINA with Encapsulate on Mina: 5% commission, no unbonding. Non-custodial.

### Mina

Delegate in two minutes. Your keys never leave your wallet; we pay your share of block rewards every two epochs.

[Delegate with Auro Wallet](https://encapsulate.xyz/guides/mina)

[Our validator](https://minascan.io/mainnet/validator/B62qjWmFMiYUiWGvisVof9mbiKi2sB1FhZdwiDyXi8nMCoLDJuFaRYY/delegations)

Withdraw today · 30 Oct

In your wallet · 30 Oct

Live dates

Slashing events

0

Since we joined

Launch

25 months

Mina does not slash stake. The line cannot break

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our blocks and votes are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

No. Mina delegates your whole balance, whatever its size; there is no partial delegation.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. They stay in your wallet — delegation is non-custodial.

How often are rewards paid?

Mina pays each block’s reward to us, not to you. We pay delegators their share, less our 5% fee, every two epochs — about 15 days.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. Mina has no slashing — a missed slot costs only that block’s reward; stake is never cut.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Nothing is locked and your MINA stays spendable; a change of delegation takes effect after one to two epochs, 7–15 days.

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed endorsement wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our endorsements and uptime are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

No. Delegate any amount the chain itself allows.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. Your NEAR sits in the pool’s contract as your stake shares; only your account can unstake or withdraw it.

How often are rewards paid?

Every epoch — about 7 hours — added to your stake.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. Below 90% uptime an epoch earns no rewards, and further down the chain removes the validator; stake is never cut.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Unstaked NEAR unlocks at the fourth epoch change — 22 to 30 hours — and earns nothing while it waits.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed attestation wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our attestations are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

No. Delegate any amount the chain itself allows.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. Your STRK sits in our delegation pool contract, and only your address can withdraw it.

How often are rewards paid?

Every epoch — about an hour — once we attest; rewards wait in the pool until you claim them.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. The chain pays nothing for an epoch without our attestation; there is no slashing.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Rewards stop the moment you ask; your STRK can be withdrawn 7 days later.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our signing and votes are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

1 SUI — the smallest stake the chain accepts.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. They stay in your wallet — delegation is non-custodial.

How often are rewards paid?

Every epoch — about 24 hours — added to your stake.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. If two-thirds of stake report a validator, the chain withholds that epoch’s rewards; stake is never cut.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Withdrawn SUI is back in your wallet at once; only the current epoch’s rewards are given up.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our signing and votes are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

Yes — 1 SUPRA, the smallest stake a delegation pool accepts.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. Your SUPRA sits in our delegation pool as shares in your name; we cannot move it.

How often are rewards paid?

Every epoch — about 2 hours — added to your stake.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. Each epoch’s reward shrinks by the share of proposals we miss; there is no slashing.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Unlocked SUPRA becomes withdrawable when the pool’s 48-hour lockup cycle ends — at most 48 hours.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our blocks and era points are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

Yes — 50 VARA to nominate us directly. Nomination pools take 1 VARA, but the pool chooses its validators.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. They stay in your wallet — delegation is non-custodial.

How often are rewards paid?

Every era — about 12 hours — once anyone claims the era’s payout; it goes to your stake or your balance, as you chose.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. Missed blocks earn nothing; if over 10% of validators are offline in a session, stake is slashed up to 7%.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Unbonding takes 7 days (14 eras); the amount earns nothing meanwhile, then you withdraw it.

What we run

#### What we run

Node operation

Bare metal, two regions, with a hot standby.

Upgrade handling

Every network upgrade since we joined, on schedule.

Monitoring

A missed block wakes someone up, at any hour.

Public record

Our signing and votes are on the explorer for anyone to check.

Common questions

#### Common questions

Is there a minimum?

Yes — 100 ZIL, our delegation contract’s minimum.

Do you hold my tokens?

No. You hold encapZIL, a liquid token worth a rising amount of ZIL; the ZIL itself sits in our delegation contract.

How often are rewards paid?

Every block, about a second — each encapZIL is worth more ZIL as they land.

What happens if you go offline?

A standby node takes over. Missed blocks earn nothing; 3 misses in 600 views bench a validator from proposing. There is no slashing.

Can I unstake at any time?

Yes. Unstaking fixes your ZIL at that moment’s price; you claim it after 461,680 blocks — about 6 days.

## Agoric staking guide

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/guides/agoric

Delegate BLD with Keplr. Seven steps across the Keplr extension and its dashboard, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

Agoric

### Delegate BLD with Keplr

Seven steps across the Keplr extension and its dashboard, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Seven screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Press Start Staking

Open Agoric in the Keplr Dashboard with your wallet connected. The Staking tab shows your BLD, how much is staked and the rewards you can claim. Press Start Staking under Your Validators.

02

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Find Encapsulate

Stake to opens on Agoric's validators, with the APR and the 21-day unstaking period at the top. Type encapsulate in the search and pick Encapsulate.

03

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Check our numbers

Encapsulate's panel shows its APR, our 9% commission, its share of voting power and the 21-day unstaking period. Press Stake.

04

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Enter an amount

Type how much BLD to stake; Max fills in your whole available balance. Press Stake.

05

of 7

In the Keplr extension

#### Unlock Keplr

The Keplr extension opens. Type your password and press Unlock.

06

of 7

In the Keplr extension

#### Approve in Keplr

Keplr shows one message, the amount of BLD to stake to Encapsulate, and a fee of a fraction of a cent. The memo is optional. Press Approve.

07

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Check the dashboard

Back on the dashboard, Staking Amount shows your stake and Your Validators lists Encapsulate with our 9% commission. Rewards build up with every block and do not compound: Claim sends them to your wallet, and Stake adds more.

Done · 7 of 7

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Delegate LUME with Keplr.

Next: Lumera

Scroll ↓

of 7

#### Open Keplr’s Axelar staking dashboard

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Find us in the list

03

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Check our numbers

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Enter an amount

of 7

In the extension

#### Unlock the Keplr wallet

of 7

In the extension

#### Approve in Keplr

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

Encapsulate · Guides

Cosmos Hub

### Delegate ATOM with Keplr

Seven steps across the Keplr extension and its dashboard, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Seven screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Press Start Staking

Open Cosmos Hub in the Keplr Dashboard with your wallet connected. The page shows your ATOM, how much is staked and the rewards you can claim. Press Start Staking under Your Validators.

02

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Find Encapsulate

Stake to opens on Cosmos Hub's validators, with the APR and the unstaking period at the top. Type encapsulate in the search and pick Encapsulate.

03

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Check our numbers

Encapsulate's panel shows its APR, our 10% commission, its share of voting power and the 21-day unstaking period. Press Stake.

04

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Enter an amount

Type how much ATOM to stake; Max fills in your whole available balance. Press Stake.

05

of 7

In the Keplr extension

#### Unlock Keplr

The Keplr extension opens. Type your password and press Unlock.

06

of 7

In the Keplr extension

#### Approve in Keplr

Keplr shows one message, the amount of ATOM to stake to Encapsulate, and a fee of a fraction of a cent. The memo is optional. Press Approve.

07

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Check the dashboard

Back on the dashboard, Staking Amount shows your stake and Your Validators lists Encapsulate with our 10% commission. Rewards build up with every block and do not compound: Claim sends them to your wallet, and Stake adds more.

Done · 7 of 7

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

## Espresso staking guide

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/guides/espresso

Stake ESP with MetaMask. Nine steps across Espresso’s staking dashboard and the MetaMask extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

Espresso

### Stake ESP with MetaMask

Nine steps across Espresso’s staking dashboard and the MetaMask extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Nine screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 9

On stake.espresso.network

#### Find Encapsulate on the dashboard

The dashboard lists every Espresso validator. Type Encapsulate in the search box and click Delegate on our row.

02

of 9

On stake.espresso.network

#### Choose MetaMask

The dashboard asks for a wallet first. Choose MetaMask from the list.

03

of 9

In the MetaMask extension

#### Connect MetaMask

MetaMask asks to connect to stake.espresso.network. Pick the account that holds your ESP and click Connect.

04

of 9

On stake.espresso.network

#### Approve ESP for staking

The delegate window opens on Encapsulate. Type the amount of ESP to stake, then click Approve.

05

of 9

In the MetaMask extension

#### Confirm the spending cap

MetaMask shows a spending cap request. It is a permission, not a payment: the most ESP the staking contract may move. Click Confirm.

06

of 9

On stake.espresso.network

#### Delegate

Back in the delegate window, check the amount reads what you want to stake, then click Delegate.

07

of 9

In the MetaMask extension

#### Confirm the delegation

MetaMask shows the transaction: the ESP you send and the network fee. Click Confirm.

08

of 9

On stake.espresso.network

#### Check the confirmation

The window reads Delegation successful, and My delegations shows your ESP. Click Close.

09

of 9

On stake.espresso.network

#### Check your delegation

The balance cards show your Total delegated, and our row lists your ESP under My delegation. Rewards accrue with every block we propose.

Done · 9 of 9

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Stake MINA with Auro Wallet.

Next: Mina

Seven steps across ping.pub and the Keplr extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Seven screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 7

On ping.pub

#### Press Delegate

Open Gravity Bridge on ping.pub and connect Keplr with the wallet button at the top right; your address and balances appear. Press Delegate.

02

of 7

On ping.pub

#### Choose Encapsulate

The Delegate window opens with your address as the sender. Open the Validator list and pick Encapsulate (10%).

03

of 7

On ping.pub

#### Enter an amount

With Encapsulate (10%) chosen, type how much to stake and press Send. Simulate only estimates the fee.

04

of 7

In the Keplr extension

05

of 7

In the Keplr extension

of 7

07

of 7

## IOTA staking guide

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/guides/iota

Stake IOTA with IOTA Wallet. Seven steps across the IOTA Wallet extension and the IOTA explorer, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

IOTA

### Stake IOTA with IOTA Wallet

Seven steps across the IOTA Wallet extension and the IOTA explorer, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Seven screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 7

In the IOTA Wallet extension

#### Unlock IOTA Wallet

Open the IOTA Wallet extension. Type your password and press Unlock wallet.

02

of 7

In the IOTA Wallet extension

#### Press Start Staking

The home screen shows your IOTA balance and the coins you hold. Press Start Staking.

03

of 7

In the IOTA Wallet extension

#### Find Encapsulate

Select a Validator opens. Type encapsulate in the search and pick Encapsulate.

04

of 7

In the IOTA Wallet extension

#### Press Next

Encapsulate's row turns grey once it is picked. Press Next.

05

of 7

In the IOTA Wallet extension

#### Enter an amount

Stake IOTA shows Encapsulate's staking APY, our 8% commission, its share of all staked IOTA and how much you already stake with it. Type how much IOTA to stake; Max fills in your whole balance. Press Stake.

06

of 7

In the IOTA Wallet extension

#### Check the transaction

Successfully sent, with Encapsulate, the IOTA you staked and the gas fee. Staking Rewards Start counts down to the next epoch, when your stake starts earning; Redeem Rewards to the epoch after, when its first rewards can be withdrawn. Press View on Explorer.

07

of 7

On explorer.iota.org

#### Check the explorer

The IOTA explorer shows the transaction as a Stake: Success, the IOTA you staked and Encapsulate, 0xedd6…c9ab. From the next epoch, rewards are added to your stake every 24 hours and compound on their own.

Done · 7 of 7

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Stake ESP with MetaMask.

Next: Espresso

Stake MINA with Auro Wallet. Nine steps in the Auro Wallet extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

Mina

### Stake MINA with Auro Wallet

Nine steps in the Auro Wallet extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Nine screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Unlock Auro Wallet

Open the Auro Wallet extension. Type your password and press Unlock.

02

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Press Staking

The home screen shows your account and the MINA you hold. Press Staking.

03

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Press Stake

Staking shows the current epoch and the time left in it, your available MINA and Lock Time: Not Locked. Press Stake.

04

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Change the validator

Stake opens with Auro's own validator, Auro Wallet, already chosen. Press it to choose another.

05

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Find Encapsulate

Block Producers lists Mina's validators. Scroll to Encapsulate and press it.

06

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Press Next

Stake now names Encapsulate as the validator. There is no amount to enter: Mina delegates your whole balance. Press Next.

07

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Confirm in Auro Wallet

Transaction Overview shows Encapsulate, its block producer address, your own address under From and a network fee of 0.0101 MINA. Press Confirm.

08

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Back to Staking

Back on the home screen, your MINA is down only by the fee: delegating moves none of it. Press Staking.

09

of 9

In the Auro Wallet extension

#### Check your stake

Staking lists Encapsulate under Active, with your whole balance staked. It counts from one to two epochs on, 7 to 15 days; from then we pay your share of the block rewards, less our 5% fee, every two epochs.

Done · 9 of 9

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Stake STRK with Ready X.

## Monad staking guide

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/guides/monad

Stake MON with MetaMask. Eleven steps across MonadVision and the MetaMask extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

Monad

### Stake MON with MetaMask

Eleven steps across MonadVision and the MetaMask extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Eleven screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### Enter the amount

Open MonadVision's MySpace on its Stake tab and type how much MON to stake; Max fills in your balance. There is no minimum.

02

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### Switch the validator

The Validator line shows MonadVision, the site's own validator, and the card stakes with whichever validator this line shows. Press its name, or the ⇄ beside it, to choose another.

03

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### Choose Encapsulate

In Choose a validator, type encap in the search and pick Encapsulate: it shows as Active, with its stake and our 15% commission.

04

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### Connect your wallet

The Validator line now reads Encapsulate, with our total stake, APR and commission. Press Connect Wallet.

05

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### Select MetaMask

In Connect a Wallet, choose MetaMask. Keplr, Phantom and the others work the same way; this guide follows MetaMask.

06

of 11

In the MetaMask extension

#### Unlock MetaMask

MetaMask opens. Type your password and press Unlock.

07

of 11

In the MetaMask extension

#### Connect to MonadVision

MetaMask shows monadvision.com and the account it will connect. The site can see your addresses and balances and send you transaction requests; it cannot move funds without your permission. Press Connect.

08

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### Press Stake

Back on MonadVision your wallet is connected, and your balance shows beside Max. With your amount in and Encapsulate on the Validator line, press Stake.

09

of 11

In the MetaMask extension

#### Confirm in MetaMask

MetaMask shows the MON you are sending, the request from monadvision.com on the Monad network and the network fee, which MetaMask may pay for you. Press Confirm.

10

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### See the confirmation

The stake lands in about a second and MonadVision shows Transaction Success. View Transaction opens it on the explorer; OK closes the notice.

11

of 11

On monadvision.com

#### Check the dashboard

Scroll down to MON Staking: Encapsulate is listed with your stake, its APR and the rewards waiting to be claimed. Rewards build up with every block we propose and do not compound: Claim sends them to your wallet, Stake adds more, and Unstake starts a withdrawal you can collect 7 to 9 hours later.

Done · 11 of 11

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Stake NEAR with Meteor.

Next: NEAR

All guides

Monad’s terms and common questions

Need help? Ask on Discord

Encapsulate · Guides

NEAR

### Stake NEAR with Meteor

Eight steps in Meteor's web wallet, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Eight screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Unlock Meteor

Open the Meteor wallet at wallet.meteorwallet.app. Type your password and press Unlock.

02

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Press Stake

Meteor opens on your account, with your NEAR under My Assets. Press Stake.

03

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Create a staking

Staking lists the pools Meteor offers by default and what you have staked so far. Press Create Staking to choose your own validator.

04

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Change the validator

Stake Your NEAR opens with Meteor Pool already chosen as the validator. Press the validator card to change it.

05

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Find Encapsulate

Select Validator opens. Type encap in the search and pick Encapsulate V2 Pool.

06

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Enter an amount

The validator card now reads Encapsulate V2 Pool. Type how much NEAR to stake; Max fills in your whole balance, so leave a little for later fees. Press Stake Now.

07

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Stake Successful

Meteor shows Stake Successful with the fee, a fraction of a cent, and the transaction ID; View on Explorer opens the transaction. Press Done.

08

of 8

On wallet.meteorwallet.app

#### Check your staking

Back on Staking, My Total Staked shows your stake and My Staking lists Encapsulate V2 Pool, `encapsulate.pool.near`. Rewards are added to your stake every epoch, about 7 hours, so they compound on their own; Stake More adds to it.

Done · 8 of 8

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Stake SUI with Slush.

Stake SOMM with Keplr. Seven steps across the Keplr extension and its dashboard, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

Sommelier

### Stake SOMM with Keplr

Seven steps across the Keplr extension and its dashboard, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Seven screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Press Start Staking

Open Sommelier in the Keplr Dashboard with your wallet connected. The Staking tab shows your SOMM, how much is staked and the rewards you can claim. Press Start Staking under Your Validators.

02

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Find Encapsulate

Stake to opens on Sommelier's validators, with the APR and the 28-day unstaking period at the top. Type encapsulate in the search and pick Encapsulate.

03

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Check our numbers

Encapsulate's panel shows its APR, 0% since Sommelier's inflation and incentives ended, our 10% commission, its share of voting power and the 28-day unstaking period. Press Stake.

04

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Enter an amount

Type how much SOMM to stake; Max fills in your whole available balance. Press Stake.

05

of 7

In the Keplr extension

#### Unlock Keplr

The Keplr extension opens. Type your password and press Unlock.

06

of 7

In the Keplr extension

#### Approve in Keplr

Keplr shows one message, the amount of SOMM to stake to Encapsulate, and a fee of a fraction of a cent. The memo is optional. Press Approve.

07

of 7

On wallet.keplr.app

#### Check the dashboard

Back on the dashboard, Staking Amount shows your stake and Your Validators lists Encapsulate with our 10% commission. Rewards build up with every block and do not compound: Claim sends them to your wallet, and Stake adds more.

Done · 7 of 7

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Delegate IXO with Keplr.

Next: ixo

## Starknet staking guide with Braavos

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/guides/starknet-braavos

Stake STRK with Braavos. Nine steps across Voyager’s staking dashboard and the Braavos extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

Starknet

### Stake STRK with Braavos

Nine steps across Voyager’s staking dashboard and the Braavos extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Nine screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 9

On voyager.online

#### Connect your wallet

Voyager’s Staking Dashboard lists every Starknet validator. Press Connect Wallet at the top right.

02

of 9

On voyager.online

#### Choose Braavos

In Select a wallet provider, choose Braavos wallet.

03

of 9

In the Braavos extension

#### Unlock Braavos

Braavos opens. Type your password and press Login.

04

of 9

In the Braavos extension

#### Connect to Voyager

Braavos asks to connect voyager.online to your wallet. Check that the account at the top is the one that holds your STRK and press Approve.

05

of 9

On voyager.online

#### Find Encapsulate

Your address now shows at the top right. Type encap in the validator search and press Stake on our row.

06

of 9

On voyager.online

#### Enter an amount

Delegate Stake opens for the validator you picked. Type how much STRK to stake, leaving a little for the fee, then press Delegate. There is no minimum.

07

of 9

In the Braavos extension

#### Sign in Braavos

Braavos shows the transaction from voyager.online: the STRK you send, under Overall balance change, and the network fee, paid in STRK. Press Sign.

08

of 9

In the Braavos extension

#### See the confirmation

Braavos shows Transaction completed. View on Explorer opens it on the explorer; OK closes it.

09

of 9

On voyager.online

#### Check your stake

Open My Activity: the delegation reads Delegated, Encapsulate, your amount and Completed, and My Stake shows your STRK. Rewards arrive every epoch, about an hour, and wait under Rewards to Claim: Claim sends them to your reward address, Restake adds them to your stake.

Done · 9 of 9

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Delegate LUNA with Keplr.

Next: Terra

All guides

Starknet’s terms and common questions

Need help? Ask on Discord

Ten steps across SuiVision and the Slush extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Ten screens

Scroll ↓

of 10

On suivision.xyz

#### Open SuiVision’s Sui staking dashboard

The dashboard shows the Sui validator list and staking details. Search for Encapsulate and open our row.

02

of 10

On suivision.xyz

#### Check our numbers

Our profile shows the staking APY, commission and total stake. Read them, then click Stake.

03

of 10

On suivision.xyz

#### Connect your wallet

Open the Stake tab and click Connect Wallet.

04

of 10

On suivision.xyz

#### Select the wallet

Choose Slush from the wallet list.

of 10

In the Slush extension

of 10

In the Slush extension

#### Connect to SuiVision

Review the connection request from SuiVision, then approve it.

of 10

On suivision.xyz

#### Enter an amount

08

of 10

In the Slush extension

#### Approve the stake

Review the transaction request. Approve it to stake your SUI with Encapsulate.

09

of 10

On suivision.xyz

The confirmation shows the amount staked with Encapsulate. Click OK to close it.

10

of 10

On suivision.xyz

#### Check your stake

Your Sui Staking row now lists Encapsulate and your staked amount. Your stake becomes active at the next epoch, within about 24 hours. Pending reward reads +0 SUI until then.

## Zilliqa staking guide

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/guides/zilliqa

Stake ZIL with Bearby. Eight steps across Zilliqa’s staking portal and the Bearby extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Encapsulate · Guides

Zilliqa

### Stake ZIL with Bearby

Eight steps across Zilliqa’s staking portal and the Bearby extension, one per screen, each with the screen you should be looking at.

Eight screens

Scroll ↓

01

of 8

On stake.zilliqa.com

#### Connect your wallet

Zilliqa’s staking portal lists its pools, liquid and non-liquid. Ours is on the Liquid tab, as Encapsulate with its token, encapZIL. Press Connect wallet.

02

of 8

On stake.zilliqa.com

#### Choose Bearby

In Connect a Wallet, choose Bearby Wallet under Installed.

03

of 8

In the Bearby extension

#### Unlock Bearby

Bearby opens. Pick your wallet, type your password and press Unlock.

04

of 8

In the Bearby extension

#### Connect to the portal

Bearby asks to connect stake.zilliqa.com to your wallet. Check that the account selected is the one that holds your ZIL and press Connect.

05

of 8

On stake.zilliqa.com

#### Find Encapsulate

Your balance and address now show at the top right, and the pools may have changed order. Pick Encapsulate on the Liquid tab.

06

of 8

On stake.zilliqa.com

#### Enter an amount

Our panel opens on Stake, with our 8% commission and what one encapZIL is worth in ZIL. Type how much ZIL to stake, at least 100, and press Stake. The line under the amount shows the encapZIL you receive.

07

of 8

In the Bearby extension

#### Confirm in Bearby

Bearby shows the transaction from stake.zilliqa.com: the ZIL you stake, sent from your account to our delegation contract, and three fee speeds, with Market picked. Press Confirm.

08

of 8

On stake.zilliqa.com

#### Check your stake

Back on the portal, our row and the panel show your encapZIL under Staked, and Last transaction opens it on the explorer. Rewards land every block and compound into encapZIL, which is worth more ZIL as they do: there is nothing to claim.

Done · 8 of 8

#### Staked with Encapsulate.

Rewards start once your stake is active. Next up: Delegate BLD with Keplr.

Next: Agoric

## Brand kit

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/brand

The Encapsulate mark, colours and type, with the rules for which file goes where. Download the kit.

Encapsulate · Brand

Assets and rules

The kit is six files, two colours and three typefaces, with one rule that decides which mark goes on which ground.

[Download the kit](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1u1i-fdr_IgiTadA-LySG4y4RjLNqUjyr?usp=drive_link)

[Read the rules](https://encapsulate.xyz/brand#block-3dee800a513881e7a304fd94a0ffc1ea)

Updated as the system changes

Scroll ↓

### Every ground, both files.

Six files, one per ground. Use the light pair on paper, the reversed pair on ink, and the green pair on the brand green — the rule behind all three is that no part of the mark may be the colour of the ground it sits on, which is why the disc and the capsule swap rather than the whole mark inverting.

01 · The marks

mark-b.svg

Click to download

wordmark.svg

mark-reversed.svg

wordmark-reversed.svg

mark-green.svg

Click to download

wordmark-green.svg

[Download the kit](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1u1i-fdr_IgiTadA-LySG4y4RjLNqUjyr?usp=drive_link)

Three grounds, two kinds

### Two brand colours.

Green is a field with black type on it — never green type on white. Click any value to copy it.

02 · Colour

The grounds

Our paper is not white and our dark sections are not black. Put the mark on these, not on #FFF or #000.

The pastel set

Graphics only — wells, covers, card fields. Never type, never a control fill.

### Three faces, one job each.

Mono is for labels, dates and figures — never a sentence. A fourth face draws the wordmark and nothing else.

03 · Type

Aa Bb Cc

Outfit

Headings · 500 – 600

Hanken Grotesk

Body · 400 – 500

Aa Bb Cc

JetBrains Mono

Labels, dates, figures · 400 – 500

And one that is not part of the system

Comfortaa

Draws the wordmark only

The letters in the wordmark are Comfortaa, and that is the only place it appears. It is never set as text — not for a heading, not for a label — and it is not needed to use the logo, because the wordmark ships as paths rather than as type. If you find yourself typing the company name in it, use the wordmark file instead.

### Clear space and minimums.

One rule, not a list of things not to do.

04 · Using it

Clear space

The height of the band inside the mark, on all four sides.

Minimum mark

24px. Below that the band closes up and it reads as a dot.

Minimum wordmark

120px wide, or the letterforms lose their terminals.

The inner gap

Transparent, not white — it takes the colour behind it.

## Privacy policy

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/privacy-policy

What we collect when you use this site, why, and what we do with it — in plain words, and as little as the site needs.

Encapsulate · Privacy

Updated 26 Sep 2026

### Privacy policy

What we collect when you use this site, why, and what we do with it — in plain words, and as little as the site needs.

Contents

- Who we are
- What we collect
- How we use it
- Who we share it with
- Cookies
- How long we keep it
- Your rights
- Changes

#### Who we are

Encapsulate runs validators on public blockchains. This policy covers encapsulate.xyz and the pages under it and our booking form. It does not cover the chains themselves: anything you sign on-chain is public by design and outside our control.

The site is run by Encapsulate Limited, a company limited by shares registered with the Innovation City Authority, Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates (registration no. 01010263, business licence no. 07010264). Registered office: Office A, Innovation City Business Centre, RAK BANK ROC Office, Ground Floor, Al Rifaa, Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. That entity is the data controller for anything described here.

#### What we collect

We collect as little as the site needs to work, and we say what each piece is for.

- Booking a call: your name, email and anything you type into the notes. Handled by Cal.com under their terms; we see the booking, not your calendar.
- Writing to us: the email you send from and what you write.
- Analytics: two, and neither sets a cookie. Super, our host, counts page views and shows us the totals. Vercel Speed Insights, which Super adds because it hosts on Vercel, measures how fast pages load — not who visits. There is no Google Analytics, Tag Manager, Meta, LinkedIn, Hotjar or Clarity on the site.
- Server logs: IP address, browser and the page requested, kept by our hosting provider under its own retention.

#### How we use it

To hold the call you booked, to answer what you asked and to keep the site running and safe. Nothing else. We do not sell, rent or trade personal data, and we do not build advertising profiles.

#### Who we share it with

Only the services that make a feature work, each bound by its own terms:

- Cal.com — scheduling the call.
- Google Workspace — our email; what you send to hello@encapsulate.xyz lands there.
- Super, on Notion, hosted on Vercel — serving the site, counting page views and keeping its server logs.
- Authorities, if the law requires it and the request is valid.

#### Cookies

The site sets no cookies. The only cookies anywhere on it come from Cal.com’s booking calendar, on the contact page and in the booking drawer: Cloudflare’s bot check (about thirty minutes) and Cal.com’s own session cookies. None of them track you across sites. If we add anything that needs consent, we will ask for it first, on the page, in plain words.

#### How long we keep it

Booking details until the call has happened and any follow-up is done, then twelve months. Correspondence for as long as the conversation is live, then twelve months. Server logs are the hosting provider’s and follow its retention.

#### Your rights

You can ask what we hold about you, ask us to correct or delete it, or object to a use. Write to the address below; we answer within thirty days. We are established in the United Arab Emirates and handle personal data under the UAE Personal Data Protection Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021). If you are in the EU or UK you also have the right to complain to your own data protection authority.

#### Changes

When this policy changes, the date at the top changes with it. We will not quietly widen what we collect.

Questions about this document

Write to [hello@encapsulate.xyz](mailto:hello@encapsulate.xyz). A person replies, usually within a few days.

## Terms of use

URL: https://encapsulate.xyz/terms-of-use

The ground rules for using this site and for delegating to a validator we run.

Encapsulate · Terms

Updated 26 Sep 2026

### Terms of use

The ground rules for using this site and for delegating to a validator we run. Short, because there is not much to say.

Contents

- What these terms cover
- Information, not advice
- Delegating to us
- Guides and tools
- Our content
- Links elsewhere
- Liability
- Changes

#### What these terms cover

These terms govern your use of encapsulate.xyz and the content on it. The site is run by Encapsulate Limited, a company limited by shares registered with the Innovation City Authority, Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates (registration no. 01010263, business licence no. 07010264). Registered office: Office A, Innovation City Business Centre, RAK BANK ROC Office, Ground Floor, Al Rifaa, Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. Delegating to a validator we run is a transaction on a public chain, governed by that chain’s protocol; it is not a contract with us, and these terms do not change that.

#### Information, not advice

Reward rates, commissions, unbonding periods and every other figure on this site describe how a chain’s protocol works, as we understand it, at the date shown. They are not financial, legal or tax advice, and they are not a promise of any return. Chains change their parameters; check the chain before you act.

#### Delegating to us

When you delegate, your tokens stay in your wallet under your keys. We never hold, move or have access to them. We run the validator; the protocol pays rewards and applies penalties. If a chain slashes our validator, the protocol may reduce delegated stake as it defines — we describe our safeguards on the Security page, but no operator can make that risk zero.

#### Guides and tools

Our staking guides, dashboards, bots and playbooks are provided as-is, to help. We test them on our own infrastructure, but we cannot know your setup. Read before you run, and keep your own keys out of anything you paste.

#### Our content

The text, diagrams and design of this site are ours. The code we publish is under the licence stated in each repository. Chain names and marks belong to their projects; we show them to identify the network, not to claim any affiliation beyond running a validator on it.

#### Links elsewhere

We link to explorers, wallets, documentation and the chains’ own sites. We do not control them and are not responsible for what they show or do.

#### Liability

To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for losses that arise from using this site, acting on its content, or delegating to a validator we run — including losses from slashing, downtime, protocol changes or market movement. Where the law does not allow a limit, it does not apply. These terms are governed by the laws of the United Arab Emirates as applied in Ras Al Khaimah, and any dispute goes to the courts there.

#### Changes

We may change these terms; the date at the top changes with them. Using the site after a change means you accept it.

Questions about this document

Write to [hello@encapsulate.xyz](mailto:hello@encapsulate.xyz). A person replies, usually within a few days.
